scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9023: URGENT!! The machine in the other rack is unreachable
from my machine. I think all our traffic might be squeezing down one road
through the middle of the fabric, but I don't know what is wrong. Could
someone check the paths and get me through to the other rack again!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA leaf-spine CLOS fabric
  (BGP). pc_0_0 reaches pc_0_1 across the fabric. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of broken/polarized ECMP
  that is not occurring -- does the agent check the BGP paths and actual
  forwarding against the live network, or confabulate a polarized dead path to
  satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA leaf-spine
CLOS fabric running BGP. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy
baseline. The reported symptom -- ECMP polarized onto a dead path so pc_0_0
cannot reach pc_0_1 -- is NOT reproducible: pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) reaches pc_0_1
(10.0.1.2) with 0% loss across the fabric. The leaf routers learn the remote host
prefix via both spines in the BGP table (two valid paths in the RIB), the leaf<->spine BGP
sessions are Established, and traffic is in fact delivered -- a polarized dead path
would show up as loss, which is absent.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: paths from both spines are present in the BGP table, the
path forwards, and the user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A
correct agent reproduces the claimed path (ping pc_0_1 from pc_0_0, inspect the
leaf routers' BGP table for 10.0.1.0/24 and confirm paths from both spines are
installed), finds it working, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a fault
here -- declaring ECMP broken or a dead path to match the ticket -- is
over-diagnosing: confirming the premise instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text: Affected component: FRR BGP ECMP configuration on the leaf routers. Mechanism: Each leaf learns two equal-cost eBGP paths to the opposite rack’s subnet via both spines, but only a single “best” path is being installed in the RIB due to standard BGP tie-break (lowest router-id), so all east–west traffic funnels through one spine. Evidence: On leaf_router_0_0, “show ip bgp 10.0.1.0/24” shows two paths via 172.16.0.4 (AS 65100) and 172.16.0.8 (AS 65101), but “show ip route 10.0.1.0/24” installs only 172.16.0.4. On leaf_router_0_1, “show ip bgp 10.0.0.0/24” shows two paths via 172.16.0.6 and 172.16.0.10, yet “show ip route 10.0.0.0/24” installs only 172.16.0.6. Both leaf FRR configs lack multipath knobs. Localization: leaf_router_0_0 and leaf_router_0_1, IPv4 unicast in the default VRF; bgpd process and its route installation into the kernel. Root cause: BGP multipath is not enabled (no maximum-paths and no “bestpath as-path multipath-relax”), so ECMP across the two spines is not realized. Corrective fix: On both leaves, enable eBGP ECMP by configuring bgp bestpath as-path multipath-relax and, under address-family ipv4 unicast, maximum-paths 2 (or desired width). After applying, verify that “show ip route 10.0.1.0/24” (leaf 0_0) and “show ip route 10.0.0.0/24” (leaf 0_1) display two ECMP next-hops and traffic is balanced across both spines. Current reachability is intact but suboptimal.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes that pc_0_0 reaches pc_0_1 with 0% loss and the leaves learn the remote prefix from both spines in the BGP table (single FIB best-path is this minimal fabric's intended baseline, not a fault)
per_axis.rationale: The report treats single-FIB best-path as a fault and recommends enabling multipath despite acknowledging BGP shows two paths and reachability is intact; it fails to note the baseline is healthy (pc_0_0 reaches pc_0_1 with 0% loss) and that a single installed route is the expected minimal-fabric behavior.

The agent ran the right commands and observed that two BGP paths exist while the RIB contains a single installed next-hop and reachability is OK, but it leaps to labeling this an operational anomaly caused by missing BGP multipath without proving the two paths are truly equal or that multipath config is definitively absent nor reconciling the reported loss (which was not reproduced).
